'A connected Mk4 must neither receive ESP32 bytes nor be awaited for an ESP32 upgrade acknowledgement' under real timing. Proven against a fake Serial whose ports are Vec<u8>. A real port that never answers is EVICTED after the 5 s read timeout (usb_serial_manager.rs:302-311), which the fake does not model.

'Preserve legitimate native-chain forwarding': that Destination::Particular's PrepareUpgrade reaches a daisy-chained ESP32 is argued from frostsnap_comms/src/lib.rs:143-155 and device/src/esp32_run.rs:378-392, not measured.

The over-limit keygen at the wire: 13-of-13 CertifyPlease is about 3,091 B and FITS the 4,096-byte frame, so no transport error will ever produce the rejection - it is a coordinator-side policy check against a declared capability. A real coordinator's reaction to the device's Refusal::GroupTooLarge at n=13 is unmeasured, and so is any end-to-end run at n=12.

Mk4 features.upgrade_digest_no_sig: true is UNREACHABLE for that profile (update_mode: false means the flag is never consulted) and is set defensively so a stray Mk4 cannot drag ESP32 peers onto the legacy message. If a Mk4 updater ever arrives, that value needs measuring rather than inheriting.

Whether real Mk4 hardware can be told apart from an ESP32 development build at all: an unregistered Mk4 is wire-indistinguishable (the only magic-bytes-time discriminator is DeviceSupportedFeatures { conch_enabled }), and closing that without a factory certificate is a bench-and-provisioning question this task does not touch and introduced no gate for.

erase_all_devices with mixed hardware: whether a daisy-chained Mk4 downstream of an addressed ESP32 forwards the DataErase cleanly and drops it is device behaviour, unexercised here. The dialog also says nothing about the skipped Mk4.

NOT bench-only and must not be cited later as measured: the evil-maid hole is untouched and open. Key 0's private key is published, so a key-0 signature is a FORMAT check and not an authorisation check; the registry changes that in neither direction and is compatibility, not permission to install.
